newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq still negotiating U.S. wheat tender - traders.
newsitem.headline: Iraq still negotiating U.S. wheat tender - traders.

text.p: Iraq is still negotiating the purchase of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter for July shipment under a United Nations monitored oil-for-food pact, European grain traders said on Monday.
The tender launched since last week has not yet led to any sales because exporters feel Iraq's offer of $194 per tonne, including cost and freight, is too low, they said.
Exporters have placed initial offers to sell the wheat at around $210-212 per tonne.
"The Iraqis made a counter-bid at $194 to some exporters but this is too low," one trader said.
But on Monday talks were still going on the basis of the $194 per tonne price, he said.
